summary: Iter155 · Phase G · UNIFIED GLOBAL SEARCH — Tested backend (15 pytest cases incl. anon 401, q-length, role-aware visibility for safety/hr/admin/pm, kinds-filter cannot expand scope, lightweight payload — no body/description/signature_image/file_data/image_data/raw, limit respected and bounds, payload echoes q+role+scope) and frontend (Cmd/Ctrl+K toggle, Esc, outside-click, click trigger, scope chip 'Scope · safety', grouped results with data-testids, ArrowDown nav, recents save after row-click and clear, mobile 375x812 panel no-overflow, input auto-focus, anonymous case unreachable in practice). Phase F SafetyShell mobile-overflow regression on CA edit dialog at 375x812 is CONFIRMED FIXED (scrollWidth==innerWidth==375, overflow=0).

issues: Radix Dialog console warning: 'DialogContent requires a DialogTitle for screen reader users.' Wrap title in VisuallyHidden or supply DialogTitle. Non-blocking but accessibility regression.

action_items: (Low) Add DialogTitle (or VisuallyHidden wrapper) to the edit-corrective-action dialog in SafetyCorrectiveActions to silence Radix a11y warning.

(Optional UX) GlobalSearch recents are only written on row-click (selectRow → pushRecent). Closing via Esc/X without selecting a row does NOT save the query. If spec intended ANY closed search to be a recent, push on closeOverlay() when q.trim().length>=2 — but current behavior (selection-only) is a reasonable choice.
critical_code_review_comments: global_search.py is clean, well-bounded, asyncio.gather'd, escapes user input with re.escape (no regex injection), excludes _id via {'_id':0} projection, and uses KIND_VISIBILITY map so scope leakage is structurally impossible — even forced ?kinds=fire_extinguishers for HR returns scope=[] total=0. Excellent permission-safe design.

GlobalSearch.jsx is well-scoped (debounce 260ms with AbortController, keyboard nav, recents keyed per-actor token, mobile-first layout). The trigger button always rendered (no hidden md:inline gating on the button itself) so mobile shells get it correctly.
Minor: KIND_TINT.document_expirations uses 'amber-50/900' while document_expirations also defaults to amber via notifications — visually similar but distinguishable by status text.

success_rate.backend: 100% (15/15 — 14 passed, 1 skipped by design when PM has no scoped project list)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (all critical flows: Cmd+K, Esc, outside-click, trigger button, scope chip, grouped results, row navigation, recents save/clear, mobile no-overflow, no console errors)
